Events.Name: Drop
Events.Doc: something with `DragData` was dropped on a widget with `AcceptDrop`. The point is in **this widget's** coordinates, and so is `Bounds(this widget)` asked of a child — so *which row a drop is over* is a comparison and not arithmetic, and on a scroller both numbers already carry the scroll (a child above the view reads a negative `Y`). A hidden child measures 0x0, so skip what is not `Visible`. Only arrives when the drop was not refused (see `DragOver`). **Undo here whatever `DragEnter` lit up**: no `DragLeave` follows a drop (see its row). Refused drops never arrive (see `DragOver`).

Events.Name: FileDrop
Events.Doc: files were dropped from the file manager or the desktop on a widget with `AcceptFiles`. `paths` is an array of full paths — **only files that have one**: a file on a remote share has no local path and does not arrive, and a drop of nothing but those is refused rather than delivered empty

Events.Name: DragEnter
Events.Doc: the drag came over a widget with `AcceptDrop`, carrying the same point `Drop` will. What the target lights up with — a column, a highlight — goes here. **The refusal does not live here**: a `false` from this one is overwritten by the very next `DragOver`, which in any real drag is immediately, so a target that refuses says so in `DragOver`

Events.Name: DragOver
Events.Doc: the drag moved over it, point after point. Where an insertion line sits is recomputed here. **Returning `false` refuses the drop at that point**: the cursor shows it and `Drop` never fires. Anything else — including answering nothing — accepts it, and with no handler everything is accepted. Strictly `false`: a handler that answers nothing returns `undefined`, which must not refuse every drag anywhere

Events.Name: DragLeave
Events.Doc: the drag left without dropping. Undoes what `DragEnter` did — **and a drop is not a leave**: measured, nothing arrives after a `Drop`, and the leave for that target is delivered at the *next* drag instead, right after its `DragBegin` and for a target that drag never touched. So a target undoes its own feedback in `Drop` as well, and anything counting enters against leaves has to expect the late one

Members.Name: Save

Events.Name: Paginate
Events.Doc: **how many sheets this document is at that size**, answered back. Raised by [`Printer`](docs/llm/library.md#printer) once the dialog has settled the paper — the only moment it can be known, and the moment the count that was declared may be wrong. `width`/`height` are the printable area in points, which is the sheet **less the printer's own margins**. It runs inside the print operation, so measure freely but **raise no events of your own** — one that re-entered the drawing hung the suite

Events.Name: Drop
Events.Doc: something with `DragData` was dropped on a widget with `AcceptDrop`. Events.Name: DragOver

Events.Name: DragLeave

Events.Name: DragLeave

The point is in **this widget's** coordinates, and so is `Bounds(this widget)` asked of a child — so *which row a drop is over* is a comparison and not arithmetic, and on a scroller both numbers already carry the scroll (a child above the view reads a negative `Y`). A hidden child measures 0x0, so skip what is not `Visible`. Only arrives when the drop was not refused (see `DragOver`). **Undo here whatever `DragEnter` lit up**: no `DragLeave` follows a drop (see its row). Refused drops never arrive (see `DragOver`).

Events.Name: FileDrop
Events.Doc: files were dropped from the file manager or the desktop on a widget with `AcceptFiles`. `paths` is an array of full paths — **only files that have one**: a file on a remote share has no local path and does not arrive, and a drop of nothing but those is refused rather than delivered empty

Events.Name: DragEnter
Events.Doc: the drag came over a widget with `AcceptDrop`, carrying the same point `Drop` will. What the target lights up with — a column, a highlight — goes here. **The refusal does not live here**: a `false` from this one is overwritten by the very next `DragOver`, which in any real drag is immediately, so a target that refuses says so in `DragOver`

Events.Name: DragOver
Events.Doc: the drag moved over it, point after point. Where an insertion line sits is recomputed here. **Returning `false` refuses the drop at that point**: the cursor shows it and `Drop` never fires. Anything else — including answering nothing — accepts it, and with no handler everything is accepted. Strictly `false`: a handler that answers nothing returns `undefined`, which must not refuse every drag anywhere

Events.Name: DragLeave
Events.Doc: the drag left without dropping. Undoes what `DragEnter` did — **and a drop is not a leave**: measured, nothing arrives after a `Drop`, and the leave for that target is delivered at the *next* drag instead, right after its `DragBegin` and for a target that drag never touched. So a target undoes its own feedback in `Drop` as well, and anything counting enters against leaves has to expect the late one

Events.Name: DragBegin
Events.Doc: on the widget being dragged: the drag started. Grey the card here

Events.Name: DragEnd
Events.Doc: on the widget being dragged: the drag finished — dropped or refused. Puts back whatever `DragBegin` changed

Events.Name: Allocated
Events.Doc: the first time GTK has given it a real rectangle — the moment `Form_Open` is reliably too early for. `box` is `Bounds()` exactly (`{X, Y, Width, Height}`, window coordinates). **Once**: a control that was already on screen has missed it, so ask `Bounds()` first when it may have. A control on a hidden page hears it when the page is shown. Nothing polls — the hook is the window's own layout pass

Members.Name: Activate
Members.Doc: raises `Activate` for that visible position, as a double click would; the selected row with no argument. Answers whether there was one. In both the flat and the tree shape, because a click lands on a position

Members.Name: ActivateOnSingleClick
Members.Doc: raise `Activate` on one click instead of two. Default `false`

Members.Name: Add
Members.Doc: one row, as an array of strings. A row shorter than there are columns reads `""` for the rest. Clears an on-demand `Count`. **`options` is `{ Key, Parent, Icon }`, and a row with a `Key` is a node**: the first one makes this table a tree, `Parent` is the key of the node it goes under (absent is a root), and `Icon` is the picture for its first column — the same one `TreeView.Add` takes, so a node need not be added and then decorated

Members.Name: AutoExpand
Members.Doc: opens a node as it arrives, and again when it gains a child after being closed by hand. Default `true`. A tree only. The same mechanism `TreeView` uses, answering the same

Members.Name: Cell
Members.Doc: one value. Refused on an on-demand table, which has no cells to answer about

Members.Name: Clear
Members.Doc: empties it — **and forgets which of the three shapes this table was**

Members.Name: CollapseAll
Members.Doc: closes every node

Members.Name: CollapseNode
Members.Doc: closes it

Members.Name: ColumnLines
Members.Doc: rules between the columns. Default `false`

Members.Name: Columns
Members.Doc: an array of `{ Text, Width, Alignment, Editable, Link }`. `Text` is **translated**; `Width: 0` sizes itself and the last column takes the slack; `Editable: true` makes a cell a field — clicked, typed and committed — and an editable column reads left-aligned, because a `GtkEditableLabel` is not a label. `Link: true` makes each cell a link — underlined, a pointer over it, a focus stop, Enter — whose address is the cell's text unless `SetUri` or `Data` says another, and a cell with no text is plain. **A column is a field or a link, never both**

Members.Name: Count
Members.Doc: how many rows — **settable**, which is the on-demand mode: the table then asks `Data(row, column)` for each cell it draws. **Settable**, and setting it is the on-demand shape. Assigning it puts the table in this shape and clears any rows it held

Members.Name: Deselect
Members.Doc: unselects it

Members.Name: DeselectAll
Members.Doc: selects nothing

Members.Name: Exists
Members.Doc: whether that node is there. `false` on a flat table rather than a refusal: it is the question you ask *before* you know

Members.Name: ExpandAll
Members.Doc: opens every node

Members.Name: ExpandNode
Members.Doc: opens or closes it. Opening opens the way to it too, since a row only exists once its ancestors are open. Not `Expand`, which is `Widget`'s layout property

Members.Name: Expanded
Members.Doc: whether it is open

Members.Name: HeaderHeight
Members.Doc: how tall the row of column headings is. `0` before the first allocation

Members.Name: HeaderMenu
Members.Doc: the menu a column heading offers on a secondary click, as the same array of items `Menu` takes. Built for each click, and every item's handler is told the column, last: `MnuHide_Click(column)`. Like `Menu`, refused on a table that is not in a form yet

Members.Name: HeaderMinHeight
Members.Doc: a floor for the row of column headings, in pixels. **The heading does not follow the control's font** -- the theme sizes it -- so this is what makes a taller one. `0`, nothing said

Members.Name: Index
Members.Doc: the selected row, `-1` for none. Assigning selects it. Default `-1`

Members.Name: Key
Members.Doc: the selected node's key; assigning selects, opening the way to it. `""` selects nothing. A tree only

Members.Name: MultiSelect
Members.Doc: more than one row at a time. Refused on a tree

Members.Name: RemoveNode
Members.Doc: takes that node out, **and the subtree with it**. **Tree only** — a flat table says `RemoveRow(index)`

Members.Name: RemoveRow
Members.Doc: takes that row out. **Flat only** — a tree says `RemoveNode(key)`, and this one refuses with that sentence

Members.Name: Reveal
Members.Doc: brings that visible row into view with the least scrolling it takes, and answers whether there was one

Members.Name: Row
Members.Doc: that row's values, as the array it was given — including any it was given beyond the columns declared. Refused on an on-demand table

Members.Name: RowHeight
Members.Doc: how tall one row is, as GTK measured it. `0` while the table holds no row or has not been laid out

Members.Name: RowLines
Members.Doc: rules between the rows. Default `true`

Members.Name: ScrollMaxY
Members.Doc: the largest `ScrollY` that still shows a row: the rows' height less one view. `0` when there is nothing to scroll

Members.Name: ScrollY
Members.Doc: how far down the rows are scrolled, in pixels -- the wheel, a scrollbar, the keyboard or an assignment. Assigning **clamps** to `[0, ScrollMaxY]`, so a number past the end means the end

Members.Name: Select
Members.Doc: move the selection from code. `Select` leaves the others alone where several are allowed

Members.Name: SelectAll
Members.Doc: with `MultiSelect`

Members.Name: Selection
Members.Doc: every selected row, as an array of indices in order

Members.Name: SetCell
Members.Doc: one cell, in place. The selection stays where it is

Members.Name: SetIcon
Members.Doc: an icon from the theme beside a cell's text. `""` takes it off. Refused on an on-demand table

Members.Name: SetUri
Members.Doc: where a `Link` cell goes when that is not its text. `""` makes the cell not a link, `null` goes back to opening its text. Refused on an on-demand table

Members.Name: SortBy
Members.Doc: actually reorders the rows it holds, **by the text the cells show**: natural order by default (`9` before `10`, the locale's collation otherwise), or `compare(a, b)` — the two cells' text, answering a number as `Array.sort`'s does — for what natural order reads wrongly: a minus sign, grouped thousands, a `d/m/Y` date. **Stable**: equal cells keep the order they had, so sorting by one column and then another nests them. A comparator that throws leaves the rows as they were

Members.Name: SortColumn
Members.Doc: the same as clicking that heading from code: the arrow moves and `Sort` is raised

Members.Name: Sortable
Members.Doc: makes the headers clickable. **The table does not reorder itself** — it raises `Sort`. Default `false`

Events.Doc: the selection moved — by the user or by an assignment. Ask `Index` for where it is and `Cell`/`Row` for what is there; `Key` when the table is a tree

Events.Name: Activate

Events.Name: Data

Events.Name: Sort

Members.Name: Members

For a member read out of a source, `Params` is counted from the parser's list by `Function.length`'s rule — the names before the first `[x]` or `...x` — so the same method answers the same count read or built. **It is the one that answers for a class that is not a widget** — `Timer`, `QrCode`, `Package` — where the three above refuse, and it takes a global that is a bag of functions (`File`, `Locale`, `Printer`) as readily as a class. A lower-case name is the class talking to itself and is not listed. **A type no global holds** — `HttpClient`, `HttpServer`, `HttpRequest`, `Connection`, `XmlDocument`, `XmlNode`, the prototypes of what a verb hands back — is answered from its table in the runtime, properties included, and a global class (`Connection`) gains what its driver adds. `options` takes **`All: true`**, which lists the lower-case names too — what a builtin like `String` or `Array` is made of — and **`Own: true`**, which answers only what the class **itself** declares: the question a reference page is written around, since what a class inherits is documented where it is declared — and **`Sources`, an array of source texts**, and **`Forms`, an array of `.form` texts**, for a class that is a lexical binding in a file this process never runs — a library's class, read by an editor that must not execute the project it is editing. The sources are read with the same parser `Application.Symbols` uses, the `extends` chain is followed, and the walk goes back to the class table at the first base the sources do not declare — which is `Form`, and a hundred names. **A class the sources declare wins over a class of the same name in the runtime**, because in a program that uses that library the library's is the class being written. A form's children are members too, and reading one needs no display: `JS_ParseJSON` and a walk of `children`, paired to the class by the form's own `class` key and not by the file's name. **They are offered for a class that is loaded as well as one only declared**, because a child is an *own property of the instance* and no prototype walk sees one either way. A lower-case child is not a member, a `.form` that does not parse is the loader's complaint rather than this verb's, and an entry that is not a string is refused; a name neither declared nor resolvable names both facts. **The source half answers in the loaded half's words**: a `static` is `Static`, a `get X` alone is `ReadOnly`, a getter with a setter is one `Property`, and a `static get` is a `Static` with `Params` `-1` — what the same class says once it is loaded. Events.Doc: files were dropped from the file manager or the desktop on a widget with `AcceptFiles`. `paths` is an array of full paths — **only files that have one**: a file on a remote share has no local path and does not arrive, and a drop of nothing but those is refused rather than delivered empty

Events.Name: DragEnter
Events.Doc: the drag came over a widget with `AcceptDrop`, carrying the same point `Drop` will. What the target lights up with — a column, a highlight — goes here. **The refusal does not live here**: a `false` from this one is overwritten by the very next `DragOver`, which in any real drag is immediately, so a target that refuses says so in `DragOver`

Events.Name: DragOver
Events.Doc: the drag moved over it, point after point. Where an insertion line sits is recomputed here. **Returning `false` refuses the drop at that point**: the cursor shows it and `Drop` never fires. Anything else — including answering nothing — accepts it, and with no handler everything is accepted. Strictly `false`: a handler that answers nothing returns `undefined`, which must not refuse every drag anywhere

Events.Name: DragLeave
Events.Doc: the drag left without dropping. Undoes what `DragEnter` did — **and a drop is not a leave**: measured, nothing arrives after a `Drop`, and the leave for that target is delivered at the *next* drag instead, right after its `DragBegin` and for a target that drag never touched. So a target undoes its own feedback in `Drop` as well, and anything counting enters against leaves has to expect the late one

Events.Name: DragBegin
Events.Doc: on the widget being dragged: the drag started. Grey the card here

Events.Name: DragEnd
Events.Doc: on the widget being dragged: the drag finished — dropped or refused. Puts back whatever `DragBegin` changed

Events.Name: Allocated
Events.Doc: the first time GTK has given it a real rectangle — the moment `Form_Open` is reliably too early for. `box` is `Bounds()` exactly (`{X, Y, Width, Height}`, window coordinates). **Once**: a control that was already on screen has missed it, so ask `Bounds()` first when it may have. A control on a hidden page hears it when the page is shown. Nothing polls — the hook is the window's own layout pass

Members.Name: Arguments
Members.Doc: whatever followed the project directory on the command line, as an array

Members.Name: CheckSource
Members.Doc: `null` when the text is valid JavaScript, else `{ Message, Line, Column }`. What an editor checks a file with before saving it, and the answer `new Function(src)` is not allowed to give

Members.Name: ConfigDirectory
Members.Doc: `~/.config/bintana/<name>`, **created at startup**, which is where anything the application remembers belongs. [`Settings`](docs/reference/globals/Settings.md) writes there; nothing of yours should go in the project directory, which is a thing people hand to each other

Members.Name: DecorationLayout
Members.Doc: how this desktop arranges a title bar — which buttons, and on which side. What a drawn title bar reads to look like the real one

Members.Name: Directory
Members.Doc: the project directory, absolute. What a relative path in a project resolves against — an image a report draws, a document a viewer opens, a data file that ships with the application

Members.Name: Executable
Members.Doc: the `bintana` binary that is running this, so a project can re-invoke it — which is how the IDE runs a project and how the test runner runs the suites

Members.Name: Globals
Members.Doc: every name on the global object: the runtime's own, the ones a library installed, and the JavaScript builtins -- `Math`, `JSON`, `Date`, `Map`, `Timer`, `Confirm`. **A top-level `class` is a lexical binding and not a property of the global object**, so a library's and a project's classes are *not* in it -- read those out of the sources, which is what the IDE does. It exists because the alternative is a hand-written list of global names, and there are a hundred and sixty-four of them

Members.Name: HasCommand
Members.Doc: whether that program is on the PATH. **The question that does not need an exception**, since [`Exec`](docs/reference/globals/Exec.md) throws when the program is not there

Members.Name: HasIcon
Members.Doc: whether that icon will actually **draw** something. Not whether the theme claims it: an icon that cannot be rasterised here is the same nothing as one that is missing

Members.Name: Icons
Members.Doc: every icon name available, sorted, narrowed by substring — what an icon picker is built from

Members.Name: Id
Members.Doc: from `project.json`: the application's identity in reverse DNS — `io.github.you.App`. It is **one name in three places**: the window's own class (the runtime hands it to `GtkApplication` for Wayland and to the program name for X11's `WM_CLASS`), the `<id>` of the project's metainfo, and the Flatpak app id. `""` when the project declares none, which is an ordinary project classed by the program's name; a value that is not an application id **stops the program when the project loads**, because every one of those three is something nobody looks at until a dock shows the wrong icon

Members.Name: Libraries
Members.Doc: the names of every library those same six places offer, sorted, each one once. The other direction of the lookup: `LibraryPath` resolves a name you already know, this is what a dialog that offers a choice needs

Members.Name: LibraryPath
Members.Doc: where a library by that name is, or `""` — **the same six-place search the runtime does for `uses`**. Published so that a tool which opens *other* projects asks about theirs rather than keeping a second copy of the path

Members.Name: Name
Members.Doc: from `project.json`

Members.Name: Quit
Members.Doc: quit with that exit status. `0` is *it worked*, and a console tool that answers a question answers with this. A `code` that is not a number is **refused** — `Quit("fail")` used to exit `0`, which a runner reads as success. A `code` that is not a number is refused rather than read as `0`, which a runner would take for success; `Quit()` is `0`

Members.Name: Replacements
Members.Doc: every name this language takes away, and what to write instead. It is a bag keyed by the name that went: `{ setTimeout: "Timer.After(delay, tick) — the delay comes first", "Object.assign": "{ ...a, ...b }", … }`. **`""` where there is no word for that thing here**, which is an answer rather than a gap in the table. An editor asks it of an identifier nobody can find, so a beginner meets `Timer` at the token rather than a `ReferenceError` at the next run

Members.Name: Symbols
Members.Returns: { Name, Kind, Line, Parent, Super, Params, End, Doc, Returns }[]
Members.Doc: what the text declares — `[{ Name, Kind, Line, Parent, Super, Params, End, Doc, Returns }]`, out of the parser and with nothing run. **`Kind` is `"Class"`, `"Function"`, `"Method"`, `"Static"`, `"Getter"`, `"Setter"`, `"StaticGetter"` or `"StaticSetter"`**, or **`"Assigned"`** (a function assigned at the top level, named by its target as written — `File.LoadJson`, `Widget.prototype.Dump` — and each function an object literal holds when the literal is assigned there, as `Target.Name`), or **`"Variable"`** (each `let`/`const`/`var`, destructured name, `for...of` variable and `catch` binding, at its line) and **`"Scope"`** (every function, anonymous ones included, with its `Params` and the lines it spans, `Line` to **`End`**; one that fails to parse spans up to where it broke) — together, what a name can mean where the cursor is — the member kinds are what separates `Value: T` from `Value(): T`, and a property of the class from one of the instance. **`Params` is the parameter list in the spelling a declaration uses** — `(message, [options], ...rest)`, `()` for a member that takes none, `""` for a class — for members and top-level functions, and **it is the function's own**: an arrow in its body or in a default value does not replace it. It is the one answer a host cannot get elsewhere, because ECMAScript discards a parameter's name at parse time and `Function.length` is a lower bound the moment one has a default. **`Super` is the name in a class's `extends`** and `""` for everything else, including an `extends` that is not a bare identifier. **`Doc` is the JSDoc comment touching the declaration** — the text before its first `@tag` — and **`Returns` the type in its `@returns {T}`**, both `""` when there is none; a comment that does not end on the line above or the same line documents nothing. What an editor lists a file with, and the answer a pattern is not allowed to guess at

Members.Name: Version
Members.Doc: what the **project** calls its release; `""` when it declares none. **`BTA_VERSION` is the runtime's** and is not this — showing the wrong one is what an About box does until it knows the difference

Members.Name: Buffering
Members.Doc: how full the buffer is, `0`…`100`. `100` is nothing to wait for — a local file never says otherwise — and less is a stream refilling, which **holds the sound while `Playing` stays true**. It is [`ProgressBar.Value`](docs/reference/widgets/ProgressBar.md)'s range, since that is where a form puts it

Members.Name: Duration
Members.Doc: seconds long, `-1` while unknown — which is always, on a live stream

Members.Name: Latency
Members.Doc: ms the RTSP jitterbuffer may hold. Default `2000`, the source's own. Read when the source is built, so a change lands on the next `Play` from a stopped player

Members.Name: Loop
Members.Doc: reseek instead of ending. A live stream cannot seek, so it ends anyway

Members.Name: Muted
Members.Doc: silence without touching `Volume`, so unmuting comes back to where it was

Members.Name: OnEnded
Members.Doc: assign `() => …`, called when it plays to the end; `null` takes it off. **Anything else is refused where it is assigned**, rather than silently never called

Members.Name: OnError
Members.Doc: assign `(message, kind) => …`; the same rule. `kind` is `NotFound`, `NotAuthorized`, `Unreachable`, `Decode` or `Error`, as a `Video`'s is

Members.Name: Password
Members.Doc: the secret beside it. **Write-only**: it reads back `""` and is never serialised, so no `.form` carries it in clear text

Members.Name: Pause
Members.Doc: holds the position

Members.Name: Play
Members.Doc: plays, and replays from the top after it ended. **Refused with no `Uri`**

Members.Name: Playing
Members.Doc: whether it is going — what `Play` asked for, until `Pause`, `Stop`, the end or an error. **Not a sample of the pipeline**, which reads as stopped mid-loop and mid-rebuffer

Members.Name: Position
Members.Doc: seconds in, `0` when unknown — which includes playing live

Members.Name: Seek
Members.Doc: jumps there. **Refused on a stream that cannot seek**, naming it

Members.Name: Seekable
Members.Doc: whether `Seek` has anything to work on. Answered once the stream is known, not when playing starts

Members.Name: Stop
Members.Doc: parks it: back to no state, the position forgotten

Members.Name: Uri
Members.Doc: what to play: a URI (`file://`, `http(s)://`, `rtsp://`) **or a plain local path**, which is turned into one. One property for both, so there is nothing to disagree. Setting it stops whatever was playing

Members.Name: User
Members.Doc: RTSP digest identity, applied to the source the playbin builds. `""` for none

Members.Name: At
Members.Doc: one byte as a number, `0`–`255`. **Throws** past the end rather than answering `undefined`

Members.Name: Concat
Members.Doc: a new one, end to end

Members.Name: Equals
Members.Doc: byte for byte. `==` compares two objects by identity, so **this is the only comparison there is**

Members.Name: FromBase64
Members.Doc: **refused, not guessed**, when the text is not that — a base64 string with a space in it is a mistake somebody should hear about

Members.Name: FromHex
Members.Doc: from hex, **refused, not guessed**, when the text is not that -- an odd number of digits or a character that is not one is a mistake somebody should hear about

Members.Name: Length
Members.Doc: how many bytes

Members.Name: Slice
Members.Doc: a new `Bytes`; **clamped** like a string's, and a negative `from` counts from the end

Members.Name: ToBase64
Members.Doc: as text; hex is lower-case, the way a digest is written

Members.Name: ToHex
Members.Doc: as hex, lower-case, the way a digest is written

Members.Name: ToText
Members.Doc: the text it is, or a **throw** when it is not valid UTF-8 — never the replacement character, which is a corruption that travels

Members.Name: Copy
Members.Doc: **immediate**: the text is on the clipboard when the call returns

Members.Name: CopyImage
Members.Doc: **immediate**: the image is on the clipboard when the call returns. `bytes` is an image GDK decodes — a PNG, a JPEG — and `QrView.ToPng()` and `DrawingArea.ToPng()` answer with exactly that

Members.Name: Paste
Members.Doc: `cb(text)` — **a callback, and it has to be**

Members.Name: PasteImage
Members.Doc: `cb(bytes)` with a PNG as [`Bytes`](docs/reference/globals/Bytes.md), or `null` when the clipboard holds no image

Members.Name: Close
Members.Doc: let it go

Members.Name: Columns
Members.Doc: `[{ Name, Type, Required, Key }]` — what is really in the table, which is how a program checks that a record's shape still fits

Members.Name: Dialect
Members.Doc: `{ Placeholder, Quote, NewKey }` — **what differs per engine**, so the portable half above can build SQL without knowing which engine it is talking to

Members.Name: Execute
Members.Doc: **one** statement, answering `{ Changes, LastId }`

Members.Name: Open
Members.Doc: whether it still is

Members.Name: Path
Members.Doc: the file this connection is

Members.Name: Query
Members.Doc: the rows a statement answers, as **plain objects** — for the report, the `GROUP BY`, the join that is not one shape

Members.Name: Script
Members.Doc: several statements and **no parameters**: a schema, a migration

Members.Name: Table
Members.Doc: a [`Table`](docs/reference/globals/Database.md): the rows of `name` as records of `Shape`

Members.Name: Tables
Members.Doc: the tables and views, ordered

Members.Name: Transaction
Members.Doc: everything in `fn` or nothing. **Nests**, through savepoints, so a function that wraps its own work in one is safe to call from inside another

Members.Name: Format
Members.Doc: rows (arrays of values) as CSV text. A value is quoted when it holds the separator, the quote, a line break or space at either end; `null` and `undefined` are empty, and a number is written as the language writes it, never in the desktop's format. `options`: `Separator` (default `,`), `Quote`, `LineEnd` (default LF)

Members.Name: Load
Members.Doc: the rows of a CSV file, as `Parse` reads them. **The error names the file**

Members.Name: Parse
Members.Doc: the rows of a CSV text, each an array of strings. `options`: `Separator` (one character; `""` or absent finds it among `,` `;` tab `|`), `Quote` (default `"`). A last line break makes no empty row

Members.Name: Save
Members.Doc: writes rows as a CSV file, as `Format` writes them

Members.Name: Sqlite
Members.Doc: opens a sqlite file -- created when it is not there -- or `":memory:"`, and answers the connection: `Query`, `Execute`, `Table` and the rest. A build without sqlite has the name and refuses, naming the package

Members.Name: Add
Members.Doc: the date `days` later. `days` may be negative, and it **refuses to leave the calendar** rather than answering something impossible

Members.Name: Between
Members.Doc: whole days from one to the other, signed

Members.Name: Today
Members.Doc: today's date as `"YYYY-MM-DD"`, at **local** midnight

Members.Name: Weekday
Members.Doc: `"Monday"` … `"Sunday"` — **a key to test against, never text to show**

Members.Name: Abs
Members.Doc: its magnitude

Members.Name: IsExact
Members.Doc: whether the value is exactly what its digits say, which a division may make false

Members.Name: Number
Members.Doc: the nearest double, asked for **by name**: for a chart, a width, a percentage — anywhere the value stops being money

Members.Name: Round
Members.Doc: `"Away"` (the default — the half goes away from zero, which is what an invoice does), `"Even"` (banker's), `"Zero"`, `"Up"`, `"Down"`

Members.Name: Scale
Members.Doc: how many decimal places it carries — `2` for money that came from `"19.99"`

Members.Name: Split
Members.Doc: pieces that add back up to the total, **exactly**

Members.Name: Trim
Members.Doc: drops trailing zeros: `2.50` → `2.5`

Members.Name: CacheDirectory
Members.Doc: `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`, or `~/.cache`. Anything that can be thrown away and rebuilt

Members.Name: ConfigDirectory
Members.Doc: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, or `~/.config`. Settings, kept apart from data because a backup or a sync usually wants one and not the other

Members.Name: DataDirectory
Members.Doc: `$XDG_DATA_HOME`, or `~/.local/share` when the desktop has not moved it. Application data that belongs to this user: a database, a saved document, an installed menu entry

Members.Name: Entries
Members.Doc: the module below

Members.Name: Directory
Members.Doc: `DataDirectory/applications`, created on first use. Write an entry there and the desktop's menu offers it; there is nothing to register and no index to update

Members.Name: Exec
Members.Doc: the value for the `Exec` key: the arguments as an array — the shape `Exec` and `Terminal.Run` already take — quoted and escaped the format's way

Members.Name: Install
Members.Doc: writes `Directory/<id>.desktop` and answers the path. Atomic — a temporary beside it, renamed over — so a failure leaves whatever was there

Members.Name: Installed
Members.Doc: the ids in `Directory`, sorted, `.desktop` removed. Only this user's: a system entry is never listed, and asking whether an entry is installed is one `includes` on this

Members.Name: Read
Members.Doc: one entry as data, exactly what `Install` takes, or `null` when there is no such file

Members.Name: Uninstall
Members.Doc: removes it, answering whether there was one. A file that is there and cannot be removed throws

Members.Name: Write
Members.Doc: the same entry and the same checks at a path the caller names, **making the directory** when it is not there. For the entry a package installs, which is not one this user's menu has; answers nothing

Members.Name: Color
Members.Doc: the desktop's colour chooser, opening on `current`. Answers an `rgb(…)`/`rgba(…)` string — **exactly what [`Background`](docs/reference/widgets/Widget.md#how-it-looks) and `Painter.Color` take**

Members.Name: OpenFile
Members.Doc: the file chooser, for something that exists

Members.Name: SaveFile
Members.Doc: the same, for somewhere to write

Members.Name: SelectFolder
Members.Doc: for a directory

Members.Name: Count
Members.Doc: how many keys

Members.Name: Entries
Members.Doc: `[{ Key, Value }, …]`

Members.Name: Has
Members.Doc: whether that key is there

Members.Name: Keys
Members.Doc: the keys

Members.Name: Values
Members.Doc: the values

Members.Name: Copy
Members.Doc: a whole tree

Members.Name: Delete
Members.Doc: an **empty** directory, as [`File.Delete`](docs/reference/globals/File.md) is

Members.Name: DeleteTree
Members.Doc: it and everything under it — the one to be careful with, and the reason it has a name of its own rather than a flag

Members.Name: Files
Members.Doc: the **full paths** of the files, sorted

Members.Name: Folders
Members.Doc: the same for the directories

Members.Name: List
Members.Doc: the **names**, sorted, with no `.` or `..` — what a tree of one folder shows

Members.Name: Make
Members.Doc: creates it **and any missing parent**, so there is no loop to write

Members.Name: Save
Members.Doc: `draw(painter, width, height)` against an image of that size, written as a PNG — `DrawingArea.Save` with the handler passed in place of the control, so it needs **no widget and no display**. Ink black, the font `Text` measures with. A `draw` that throws writes no file, and the throw is this call's

Members.Name: SavePdf
Members.Doc: `draw(painter, page, width, height)` once per page into one **PDF** — `DrawingArea.SavePdf` with the drawing passed in place of the control, and `DrawPage`'s own arguments. The size is in **points**, 72 to the inch (A4 is 595×842); `pages` may be `undefined` for one. What a `main` project prints with: **no widget and no display**. A page that throws leaves **no file**

Members.Name: ToPng
Members.Doc: the same picture as `Save`, answered as `Bytes` instead of written

Members.Name: CurrentDirectory
Members.Doc: where the process is. **Assigning enters it, and throws if there is no such directory** — a failure worth hearing about, since everything relative afterwards would otherwise be wrong

Members.Name: Get
Members.Doc: the variable, or `null` — which is the difference between *empty* and *not set*, and both happen

Members.Name: HasDisplay
Members.Doc: whether there is a screen at all — what a tool that may run over ssh asks before opening a window. It asks the environment (`DISPLAY`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`), not this process

Members.Name: HomeDirectory
Members.Doc: the user's home

Members.Name: HostName
Members.Doc: and on which machine

Members.Name: OS
Members.Doc: which operating system

Members.Name: OSVersion
Members.Doc: and which version of it

Members.Name: ProcessId
Members.Doc: this process's id, for a scratch name that two runs will not share

Members.Name: ProcessorCount
Members.Doc: how many cores — for the `-j` of a build, and little else

Members.Name: Set
Members.Doc: sets one; `null` **removes** it. It is `export`, so it affects everything started **afterwards** and nothing already running

Members.Name: TempDirectory
Members.Doc: where a temporary file belongs

Members.Name: UserName
Members.Doc: who is running it

Members.Name: Variables
Members.Doc: all of them at once, as an object

Members.Name: Wait
Members.Doc: runs it and **waits**, answering what it printed: `{ ExitCode, Output }`. It blocks the main loop, so it is for programs that answer in milliseconds -- `msgfmt`, `git rev-parse`, `which` -- and never for one that might sit there; `Input` is the text or `Bytes` the child reads, which is what makes `Exec.Wait(["sort"], { Input: text })` a filter

Members.Name: Bool
Members.Doc: `true`/`false`, and SQL's `0`/`1`; `def` is where it starts

Members.Name: Bytes
Members.Doc: a [`Bytes`](docs/reference/globals/Bytes.md) — a file in a record. Options: `required`, `max` (bytes)

Members.Name: Date
Members.Doc: `"YYYY-MM-DD"`, checked against the calendar. Options: `required`

Members.Name: DateTime
Members.Doc: `"YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM"` or `"...:SS"` — a date and a time — with `Z` or `+HH:MM` when the moment has a zone, kept as written. Options: `required`, `min`, `max` (local time only)

Members.Name: Decimal
Members.Doc: a [`Decimal`](docs/reference/globals/Decimal.md) at a fixed scale. Options: `required`, `min`, `max`, `decimals` (2 by default)

Members.Name: Enum
Members.Doc: one of `values`, starting at `def`. Options: `required`

Members.Name: Int
Members.Doc: a whole number. Options: `required`, `min`, `max`

Members.Name: List
Members.Doc: an array, each entry through `item` — a `Field` or a `Record` class. Options: `required`, `max`

Members.Name: Number
Members.Doc: a number. Options: `required`, `min`, `max`, `decimals`

Members.Name: Record
Members.Doc: another record: the class, or `() => the class` for a shape that contains itself. Starts at `null`. Options: `required`

Members.Name: Text
Members.Doc: a string. Options: `required`, `max` (characters)

Members.Name: Time
Members.Doc: `"HH:MM"` or `"HH:MM:SS"`. Options: `required`, `min`, `max`

Members.Name: Absolute
Members.Doc: the path resolved against the working directory

Members.Name: Append
Members.Doc: adds `text` to the end, and creates the file when it is not there. A log or a CSV written line by line wants this: `Save(path, Load(path) + line)` is the whole file through memory for every line, and a window in which another writer's line is overwritten

Members.Name: BaseName
Members.Doc: `/a/b/c.js` → `c`

Members.Name: Copy
Members.Doc: **byte for byte**, so it works on images; refuses to clobber

Members.Name: Delete
Members.Doc: a file, or an **empty** directory. Throws on failure

Members.Name: Exists
Members.Doc: `false` for anything that is not a string, rather than asking about a file called `undefined`

Members.Name: Extension
Members.Doc: `js` — no dot, `""` when there is none

Members.Name: Hash
Members.Doc: the checksum as hex, `"Sha256"` unless told — see [`Hash`](docs/reference/globals/Hash.md). **Read in blocks**, so a video costs 64 KB of memory and not the video

Members.Name: Info
Members.Doc: `{ Size, Modified, Type, Icon, IsDir }`, or `null`. `.Type` is a content type you can test (`"image/png"`), `.Icon` is the name the desktop draws for that kind of file, and `.Modified` is a real `Date`, to the millisecond

Members.Name: IsDir
Members.Doc: whether it is a directory — the question to ask before [`Directory`](docs/reference/globals/Directory.md)'s three verbs, which throw on anything else

Members.Name: IsExtension
Members.Doc: whether the name ends in that extension, **case-insensitively**. `"js"` and `".js"` are both taken, and a suffix like `"tar.gz"` is refused: the extension is what [`Extension`](docs/reference/globals/File.md#paths) answers, which stops at the last dot

Members.Name: Join
Members.Doc: one path out of pieces, with the separator the platform uses

Members.Name: Load
Members.Doc: the whole file as a string. **Throws if it cannot be read**, and the message names the file: there is no `null` to test for and no silent empty string

Members.Name: LoadBytes
Members.Doc: the whole file as [`Bytes`](docs/llm/library.md#bytes), untouched — what `Load` cannot do, since it answers text

Members.Name: LoadJson
Members.Doc: the file, parsed. **The error names the file**, which is the whole reason to use it over `JSON.parse(File.Load(p))` — a syntax error in *something* is not an answer

Members.Name: LoadXml
Members.Doc: the file as a [`Xml`](docs/reference/globals/Xml.md) document. **The error names the file**, and the document's own declaration says what encoding it is in: this reads bytes, unlike `Load`

Members.Name: Name
Members.Doc: `/a/b/c.js` → `c.js`

Members.Name: Open
Members.Doc: hands the file to whatever the desktop opens that kind with. **It answers before the file is open**: launching is asynchronous and the program that opens it is somebody else's, so what this promises is that the request was made. A file that is not there is refused *here*, which is the failure a caller can do something about

Members.Name: Relative
Members.Doc: `path` with `root` taken off; the path unchanged when there is no relative spelling, and `""` for the root itself

Members.Name: Rename
Members.Doc: also moves; refuses to clobber

Members.Name: Save
Members.Doc: writes it **atomically** — a temporary beside it, renamed over — so a failed write leaves the old file intact and a reader never sees half a file

Members.Name: SaveBytes
Members.Doc: those bytes, exactly; the pair of `LoadBytes`

Members.Name: SaveJson
Members.Doc: one canonical shape: indented by two, one trailing newline. Every `.form` and every `project.json` in this tree is written by it, which is why a file saved by the IDE and one written by hand look the same

Members.Name: SaveXml
Members.Doc: the canonical XML shape, atomically, honouring neither locale nor encoding guesses

Members.Name: Trash
Members.Doc: to the desktop's trash, whole for a folder. Throws where there is no trash

Members.Name: Watch
Members.Doc: `cb(event, path)` — `"Changed"`, `"Created"`, `"Deleted"` — and answers something with a `Stop()`

Members.Name: Within
Members.Doc: whether `path` is `root` or under it, by whole path components — `/a/proj2` is **not** inside `/a/proj`

Members.Name: Compress
Members.Doc: `data` (text as its UTF-8, or a [`Bytes`](docs/llm/library.md#bytes)) as one gzip member. `Level` is 1 (fast) to 9 (small), 6 unless told. A second option, or a value that is neither text nor `Bytes`, is refused. About 50 MB a second: a big one belongs in a [`Task`](docs/llm/library.md#task)

Members.Name: CompressFile
Members.Doc: gzips a file into another **without loading it**, 64 KB at a time, and answers the bytes written. The destination appears only when it is whole: a failure leaves no half-written file, and an existing one is untouched

Members.Name: Decompress
Members.Doc: what `bytes` holds, **all of it**: members glued together are read to the end, a stream that stops inside one **throws** (naming how far it got) rather than answering what it had, and so does anything that is not gzip. The answer may not pass `MaxSize` bytes (256 MiB unless told), because a few kilobytes can inflate to gigabytes. Text comes out as `ToText()` of the answer

Members.Name: DecompressFile
Members.Doc: the reverse, streamed, with the same ceiling and the same promise about the destination. Answers the bytes written

Members.Name: Hmac
Members.Doc: the keyed digest (RFC 2104) as lower-case hex, `"Sha256"` unless told. `key` and `message` are text (its UTF-8) or a [`Bytes`](docs/llm/library.md#bytes), and **nothing else**: a number or `undefined` is refused rather than signed as the word it spells. For a signature somebody sent you, **do not compare the answer with `===`** -- that is what `Verify` is for

Members.Name: Md5
Members.Doc: the MD5 digest. Old and broken for anything adversarial; fine for a cache key or an etag somebody else chose. `v` is text (hashed as its UTF-8) or a [`Bytes`](docs/llm/library.md#bytes) (hashed as the bytes it is)

Members.Name: Sha1
Members.Doc: likewise, and likewise

Members.Name: Sha256
Members.Doc: **the one to reach for** unless something else decided

Members.Name: Sha512
Members.Doc: when what you are comparing against used it

Members.Name: Verify
Members.Doc: whether `signature` is the keyed digest of `message`, compared in constant time. `signature` is hex (either case) or a [`Bytes`](docs/llm/library.md#bytes) of the raw digest; text that is not hex of the right length is `false`, not an error, since it is what a forged one looks like. Never answers by throwing for a wrong signature

Members.Name: Client
Members.Doc: a client with its own session: `BaseUrl`, `Headers`, `Timeout` (ms, `0` waits forever), `FollowRedirects` (default `true`), `Language`, `UserAgent`, `Proxy`, `Auth`, `Cookies`, `IdleTimeout`, `MaxConns`, `MaxPerHost`. The options are an object — a bare URL is refused

Members.Name: Delete
Members.Doc: no body, like `Get`

Members.Name: DeleteWait
Members.Doc: the blocking `Delete`

Members.Name: Get
Members.Doc: the ordinary read

Members.Name: GetWait
Members.Doc: the blocking `Get`

Members.Name: Head
Members.Doc: the headers and no body, for *is it there* and *has it changed*

Members.Name: HeadWait
Members.Doc: the blocking `Head`

Members.Name: Patch
Members.Doc: the same, for part of one

Members.Name: PatchWait
Members.Doc: the blocking `Patch`

Members.Name: Post
Members.Doc: `body` is text, [`Bytes`](docs/reference/globals/Bytes.md), an object (canonical JSON, `application/json`) or a [`Multipart`](docs/reference/globals/Http.md#uploads)

Members.Name: PostWait
Members.Doc: the blocking `Post`

Members.Name: Put
Members.Doc: the same, for a replacement

Members.Name: PutWait
Members.Doc: the blocking `Put`

Members.Name: Request
Members.Doc: any verb: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`; anything else is refused, in the blocking spelling too

Members.Name: RequestWait
Members.Doc: the blocking spelling: answers with the record, **throws** on transport failure — and what it throws carries the same `Kind` and `Status` the callback would have been handed

Members.Name: Server
Members.Doc: a listener of its own, for a static file server, a local API, a callback endpoint. Everything about it is on [`HttpServer`](docs/reference/globals/HttpServer.md)

Members.Name: Stream
Members.Doc: the answer **as it arrives**: `onLine(line, handle)` once per text line, the newline stripped, blank lines included. Method-first like `Request`, so a `POST` whose answer comes in pieces needs no second name

Members.Name: Available
Members.Doc: whether this build has libsecret. It says nothing about whether the machine is running a secret service -- a headless session has none -- so a caller treats a failed `Lookup` like an empty vault

Members.Name: Delete
Members.Doc: forgets it, and calls `cb(ok)`: `false` when there was nothing under those names or the vault could not be asked. Deleting what is not there is not an error

Members.Name: Lookup
Members.Doc: reads what `Store` saved, and calls `cb(value)` -- the text, or `null` when nothing is stored **or** the vault cannot be asked

Members.Name: Store
Members.Doc: puts `value` in the system's keyring under `service` and `key`, and calls `cb(ok)` when the vault answers -- `false` when it could not store it, which is what a machine with no secret service says. The label a keyring browser shows is made of the two names

Members.Name: Available
Members.Doc: the catalogue names this project ships, sorted — what a language menu is built from

Members.Name: Compare
Members.Doc: `-1`, `0` or `1`, in the order this desktop puts names in. `localeCompare` is **refused** and its message points here: it compares code units and puts `Álvarez` after `Zapata`

Members.Name: Context
Members.Doc: gettext's `msgctxt`, for the word that is not translated the same way twice — *Open* the verb on a button and *Open* the state of a file. The context is part of the key and is never shown

Members.Name: Currency
Members.Doc: money, with the symbol where this desktop puts it — which is before the number in some places and after it in others

Members.Name: Current
Members.Doc: which catalogue is in use, `""` for none. **Assigning reloads it, and affects only what is built afterwards** — a form already on screen keeps the words it was built with

Members.Name: Date
Members.Doc: `"Date"` `"Time"` `"DateTime"` `"ISO"` `"Weekday"` `"Month"`. `when` is a `Date` **or** a `"YYYY-MM-DD"` string

Members.Name: DecimalPoint
Members.Doc: the character a decimal is written with here, for the rare case that has to parse one back

Members.Name: Matches
Members.Doc: whether a search for `needle` should find `text`, **accents folded**: `cordoba` finds `Córdoba` and `ver` finds `Echeverría`. `toLowerCase().includes()` does neither

Members.Name: Number
Members.Doc: grouped, with this desktop's separators. As many decimals as the value has, unless told

Members.Name: Parse
Members.Doc: a [`Decimal`](docs/reference/globals/Decimal.md), or `null` when the text is not a number. **`null` and not a throw**: a field being typed into is not an error. The same format read backwards

Members.Name: Plural
Members.Doc: the form `n` takes **by the catalogue's own rule** — which is not *one or many* in every language, and is why this is not an `if` you write yourself. `n` also fills `{0}`

Members.Name: Read
Members.Doc: a catalogue as data, losing nothing: entries, contexts, plurals, comments and the fuzzy flags. What a translation editor reads

Members.Name: Text
Members.Doc: the catalogue's version of a string, with `{0}`, `{1}` filled in from the arguments. **The msgid itself when there is no entry**, so an application with no catalogue at all still reads correctly

Members.Name: Write
Members.Doc: those entries back as a `.po` — the same shape `Read` answers with, so the two are one pair. **Nothing is lost in either direction**, which is what makes an editor built on them safe on a file it only half understands. The two are one pair: what the reader kept, the writer writes

Members.Name: Hold
Members.Doc: runs `fn` with the named lock held and releases it — whether `fn` returned, threw, or was interrupted. Answers nothing

Members.Name: Debug
Members.Doc: the detail that is only interesting when something is wrong

Members.Name: Error
Members.Doc: what failed

Members.Name: Info
Members.Doc: what the program did

Members.Name: Level
Members.Doc: the floor — lines below it are dropped, which is how a program ships with its `Debug` lines still in it

Members.Name: Target
Members.Doc: where the lines are written: `"Terminal"` (the default, and stdout/stderr under it), `"Journal"` where the build has one, or **a file path** — opened in append mode and flushed per line, and it reads back as the path

Members.Name: Warning
Members.Doc: what it did not like but carried on through

Members.Name: Error
Members.Doc: something failed; the same as `Info` in every other respect

Members.Name: Info
Members.Doc: something happened. **It shows and returns**: it does not block and there is no answer. The text goes through the catalogue with `{0}` holes filled from the arguments -- never a template literal -- and with no display it prints to stderr

Members.Name: Warning
Members.Doc: something is not right; the same as `Info` in every other respect

Members.Name: Field
Members.Doc: one text part; answers the upload, for chaining

Members.Name: File
Members.Doc: one file part; `body` is text or [`Bytes`](docs/reference/globals/Bytes.md), `application/octet-stream` unless told

Members.Name: Length
Members.Doc: how many parts

Members.Name: Part
Members.Doc: one part read back: `{ Name, Filename, Type, Data }`, `Data` as `Bytes`. Past the end is refused

Members.Name: Send
Members.Doc: shows a desktop notification and answers its id. With no body, the second argument may be the options: `{ Id, Urgency, Icon }`. `Urgency` is `"Low"`, `"Normal"` (the default), `"High"` or `"Urgent"`; `Icon` is a theme icon name; sending again with the same `Id` **replaces** what is showing. The title and body are not looked up in a catalogue -- wrap them in `Locale.Text`. Refused in a project with a `main`, which has no application to send from

Members.Name: Withdraw
Members.Doc: takes a notification back, by the id `Send` answered or was given. An id nothing is showing under is not an error

Members.Name: Antialias
Members.Doc: smooth edges. Default `true`. **The one performance knob**: a line that crosses its own height on every segment costs 109 ms antialiased and 7.8 ms without, measured — the cost is in pixels covered, not in points

Members.Name: Arc
Members.Doc: **angles in degrees**, clockwise, zero at three o'clock. Appends to the path, so a pie slice is `MoveTo` the centre, `Arc`, `ClosePath`, `Fill`

Members.Name: ArcNegative
Members.Doc: the same arc counter-clockwise. **A ring needs it**: a doughnut segment is the inner start, `Arc` out and round, then `ArcNegative` back along the inner radius — one path. Going back with a `MoveTo` makes a second subpath, and filling two subpaths cuts wedges through the shape

Members.Name: Clip
Members.Doc: clip to the current path

Members.Name: ClipRectangle
Members.Doc: the common case of it

Members.Name: ClosePath
Members.Doc: back to where the path started

Members.Name: Color
Members.Doc: any CSS colour, the same spelling `Background` takes (`"rgba(53,132,228,0.2)"`). Reads back the string it was given; before anything is set, the theme's ink

Members.Name: CurveTo
Members.Doc: a cubic Bézier: two control points and the end

Members.Name: Dark
Members.Doc: whether the ground is dark, derived from the ink's luminance. What a palette is chosen by

Members.Name: Fill
Members.Doc: fill the path, and clear it

Members.Name: Font
Members.Doc: a Pango description (`"Cantarell Bold 10"`). Defaults to the widget's, so a drawing follows the desktop's font and text scale

Members.Name: Foreground
Members.Doc: the colour this widget's text is drawn in, resolved — the theme's, or the control's own `Foreground` if a form set one. The one fact a drawing cannot work out for itself. A *change* to it reaches the painter a turn later

Members.Name: Image
Members.Doc: a picture, put down with its top-left corner there. **One of `width`/`height` is enough** — the other follows the image's own proportions. With neither it is drawn at its natural size, one image pixel to one. A **string** is a file, absolute or relative to the working directory; **`Bytes`** are the image itself, which is what `Http` answers with. Missing, or not an image, **throws** and ends the frame. A path is decoded once and cached, so a drawing may paint the same logo every frame; **bytes are decoded on every call** — the cache is keyed on the path, and bytes have no key that stays true. Measured: 2.7 ms a call for a 640×480 PNG against 0.045 ms for the same file cached. A handler painting the same bytes every frame wants a `Picture` with `LoadBytes` instead

Members.Name: LineCap
Members.Doc: `Butt` `Round` `Square`

Members.Name: LineDash
Members.Doc: an array of lengths, `[]` for solid

Members.Name: LineJoin
Members.Doc: `Miter` `Round` `Bevel`

Members.Name: LineTo
Members.Doc: a segment

Members.Name: LineWidth
Members.Doc: in pixels. Default `1`

Members.Name: MoveTo
Members.Doc: start somewhere

Members.Name: Polygon
Members.Doc: the same, closed

Members.Name: Polyline
Members.Doc: a flat array — `[x, y, x, y, …]` — as one call. Worth about 2× over a loop of `LineTo`, measured, because filling the array costs what the calls would

Members.Name: Pop
Members.Doc: back to the last `Push`

Members.Name: Push
Members.Doc: remember the colour, the pen, the transform and the clip

Members.Name: Rectangle
Members.Doc: into the path

Members.Name: Rotate
Members.Doc: degrees, like `Arc`

Members.Name: Scale
Members.Doc: one argument scales both

Members.Name: Stroke
Members.Doc: stroke the path, and clear it

Members.Name: Text
Members.Doc: the text with its top-left corner there, in `Font`. Leaves no path behind. `options` is `{ Width, Markup, Align }` — see below

Members.Name: TextHeight
Members.Doc: how tall it would be. A chart asking for a line's height passes `"0"`; the same options, so a wrapped or styled run measures as what it will be

Members.Name: TextWidth
Members.Doc: how wide it would be, which is how a label is right-aligned

Members.Name: Translate
Members.Doc: move the origin

Members.Name: Close
Members.Doc: closes it. Nothing happens when it is not open; `Closed` is called once it is down

Members.Name: IsOpen
Members.Doc: whether `Show` opened it and it has not closed since

Members.Name: Show
Members.Signature: (content, anchor, [{ Rect, Position, Arrow, Autohide, Closed }])
Members.Doc: opens `content` — any control, usually a component with a `.form` of its own — floating over `anchor`. **Not in the form's tree**: it takes no room, appears in no `Children`, and nothing in the form being drawn mentions it. A control that is in a container is taken out of it, as `Add` would; it comes back out, free-standing, when the popover closes, and can be shown again. The options: `Rect` (`{ X, Y, Width, Height }` in the anchor's own coordinates — what `Editor.CursorBounds()` answers — points at a place in it instead of the whole of it), `Position` (`Top`, `Bottom`, `Left` or `Right`, the side it **prefers**; default `"Bottom"`), `Arrow` (the tail pointing back at the anchor, default `true`; `false` for a list flush against a field), `Autohide` (a click outside or Escape closes it, default `true`) and `Closed` (a function called once when it went down, **by any road**, the window going included). A misspelt option is refused. Showing a control that is already open moves it, with the options given this time. The anchor must be on screen, which it cannot be before the window is shown. The point is taken once: an anchor that moves afterwards leaves the popover where it opened

Members.Name: Default
Members.Doc: the one it would use. `""` when none is marked, **`null`** when it cannot ask

Members.Name: Names
Members.Doc: the printers this session can reach. `[]` for a machine with none, **`null`** for a session that cannot ask

Members.Name: Papers
Members.Doc: `{ A4: { Width, Height }, Letter: …, A5: … }`, in **points**. Read off GTK, so a size that reads 595 here is the 595 the print context hands the handler

Members.Name: Send
Members.Doc: the print dialog, then a printer. **Async**: it returns at once and `cb({ Copies, From, To })` arrives when something was printed. The setup is what the dialog **opens on**

Members.Name: ToFile
Members.Doc: the same sheets as one PDF, with **no dialog**; → how many pages it wrote. `Copies` is refused here, because a file has none

Members.Name: Image
Members.Doc: the picture's pixels, from its header. `null` when `path` is not a picture this machine's loaders read -- exactly the files a `Picture` would not show, an `.svg` included where no SVG loader is installed, and its declared size where one is -- or is not there. **A file's header and nothing else**: the size of a picture already in memory is the handle's to answer, off the decode it already did. **No widget and no display**, which is what makes it answerable in a `main` project and before anything has been drawn

Members.Name: Active
Members.Doc: whether the marks are going anywhere: true while this run is under Sysprof or was started with `--profile`. False in an ordinary run, where `Begin`/`End`/`Mark` do nothing at all

Members.Name: Begin
Members.Doc: opens a span on the timeline. `End(name)` closes it and the pair becomes one mark of the whole stretch — what an application uses around its own work (loading, computing, laying out), since a sampled profile cannot say which of its functions was running. Inert when `Active` is false

Members.Name: Counter
Members.Doc: one number on a track of its own — rows loaded, items in a cache, a queue's depth — defined the first time the name is seen and updated after, so a capture shows it as a graph beside the marks. The capture keeps 31 characters of the name; the value is a number, and one that is not finite is refused even with nobody listening, because a typo should not wait for a capture. Inert when `Active` is false

Members.Name: End
Members.Doc: closes the innermost `Begin`, which has to be the same name. A `name` that does not match is refused naming both, since a span closed in the wrong order would put one name's time on another's. Inert when `Active` is false

Members.Name: Mark
Members.Doc: one instant on the timeline with no duration — a point in the program rather than a stretch. Inert when `Active` is false

Members.Name: Bytes
Members.Doc: `count` bytes from the operating system's source, 0 to 1,048,576. **The one to make a token, a key or a nonce from** -- `Math.random` is not. Throws, and never falls back to something weaker, if the system has no randomness to give

Members.Name: Int
Members.Doc: a whole number from `min` to `max`, **both ends included**, every value exactly as likely. Throws for ends that are not whole numbers, for `min` above `max`, and for a range wider than 2^53

Members.Name: Uuid
Members.Doc: a version 4 UUID in its lower-case 8-4-4-4-12 spelling, from the same source as `Bytes`. Random, so it does not sort by creation: as a database key it scatters an index

Members.Name: Apply
Members.Doc: assigns each property of a plain object to the field of the same name, through the fields' own checks

Members.Name: Clone
Members.Doc: a copy, which is what a dialog edits so that Cancel costs nothing

Members.Name: Dump
Members.Doc: prints what it holds

Members.Name: Load
Members.Doc: a record from a file's object, read **leniently**: what fits is taken and what does not is reported in `Problems`

Members.Name: LoadXml
Members.Doc: the same as `Load`, from an XML document or element, by the shape's `static Xml`

Members.Name: Problems
Members.Doc: **the report of one `Load`**: what the file said that could not be taken

Members.Name: PropertyInfo
Members.Doc: `{ Kind, Column, Key }`: what a field *is*, for whoever maps it onto something else

Members.Name: PropertyNames
Members.Doc: the fields, as a widget answers its properties

Members.Name: PropertyOptions
Members.Doc: the values a field accepts, as a widget answers them — an `Enum`'s list

Members.Name: SaveXml
Members.Doc: writes into that element, touching **only** what the shape models

Members.Name: Serialize
Members.Doc: a plain object — **what differs from the start**, or everything with `true`

Members.Name: ToXml
Members.Doc: a new element: what differs from the start, or every field

Members.Name: Validate
Members.Doc: what is wrong with what the record holds **now** — a different question, and the one a form asks before saving

Members.Name: Escape
Members.Doc: the text as a **literal** inside a pattern

Members.Name: IsMatch
Members.Doc: whether it matches at all

Members.Name: Match
Members.Doc: the first match at or after `start`, or `null`

Members.Name: Matches
Members.Doc: every match, for a `for…of`

Members.Name: Pattern
Members.Doc: the pattern, as it was written

Members.Name: Replace
Members.Doc: the text with the matches replaced. **All of them** unless a count says how many

Members.Name: Split
Members.Doc: the pieces between the matches

Members.Name: Height
Members.Doc: its height, likewise

Members.Name: Monitors
Members.Doc: every monitor: `X`/`Y` are where it sits in the desktop's coordinates, `Width`/`Height`/`Scale` are its own, and `Name` is the connector — `"HDMI-1"`, `"eDP-1"` — **a key to remember a choice by, not prose to show**

Members.Name: Scale
Members.Doc: that monitor's scale factor, `1` unless the panel is HiDPI

Members.Name: Width
Members.Doc: the width of the monitor the application's **active window** is on — the first one the display lists before any window is shown, and `0` with no display at all

Members.Name: Clear
Members.Doc: forgets every value, and writes the file

Members.Name: Delete
Members.Doc: forgets the value under `key`, and writes the file

Members.Name: Get
Members.Doc: the value under `key`, or `fallback` when there is none — which is what tells a missing setting from one that is `false`

Members.Name: Has
Members.Doc: whether there is a value under `key`

Members.Name: Keys
Members.Doc: every key there is a value under

Members.Name: Path
Members.Doc: where the settings are kept: `Application.ConfigDirectory/settings.json`

Members.Name: Set
Members.Doc: stores `value` under `key`, anything JSON carries, and writes the file at once

Members.Name: Elapsed
Members.Doc: milliseconds, **with the fraction**, running or not

Members.Name: Reset
Members.Doc: back to zero, running or not; answers the watch

Members.Name: Running
Members.Doc: whether it is going

Members.Name: Start
Members.Doc: starts measuring, or goes on from where it stopped; answers the watch

Members.Name: Stop
Members.Doc: stops measuring and keeps `Elapsed`; answers the watch

Members.Name: All
Members.Doc: every row, as records

Members.Name: Connection
Members.Doc: the connection it came from

Members.Name: Count
Members.Doc: a number, building no records

Members.Name: Delete
Members.Doc: DELETE by key; **throws** when it matched no row

Members.Name: Find
Members.Doc: one record or `null`; one value per key field, in declaration order

Members.Name: Insert
Members.Doc: INSERT, and tells the record its new key

Members.Name: Name
Members.Doc: the table's name

Members.Name: Save
Members.Doc: `Insert` when the key is at its starting value, else `Update`

Members.Name: Shape
Members.Doc: the record class it maps

Members.Name: Update
Members.Doc: UPDATE by key; **throws** when it matched no row

Members.Name: Where
Members.Doc: the filter is **SQL**; anything after it (`ORDER BY`, `LIMIT`) goes too

Members.Name: Report
Members.Doc: the worker's voice, called from `Run`; arrives as `Progress`. `this.Report` on a proxy is refused

Members.Name: Start
Members.Doc: serialises the message, loads the class's file in a fresh runtime on a fresh thread, builds the class, and calls `Run(msg)`. **Once** — a second `Start` is refused; work that repeats is a new `Task`

Members.Name: Stop
Members.Doc: **asks** it to end, and enforces `KillAfter` ms later (5000 by default, 0 = at once). Two stages like `Exec`'s guard. Answers whether there was a live job to ask

Members.Name: Stopping
Members.Doc: inside `Run`: `true` once `Stop()` has asked, so the job can `Report` what it has and return. Delphi's `Terminated`, BackgroundWorker's `CancellationPending`

Members.Name: Bounds
Members.Doc: the rectangles covering those characters: `{ X, Y, Width, Height }`, one per line the range crosses and more than one on a line that changes direction

Members.Name: Escape
Members.Doc: the text as markup that says exactly it: `&`, `<` and `>` escaped

Members.Name: Font
Members.Doc: the desktop's UI font, which is what a control draws with unless CSS says otherwise. Where there is no desktop to ask — a `main` project — GTK's own default, `"Sans 10"`, which is what `Drawing` draws in

Members.Name: Height
Members.Doc: how tall — one line's height, or the whole block's when it wraps

Members.Name: IndexAt
Members.Doc: which character is at that point, as an index into the text **as it was laid out** — a markup run's tags already consumed. Above the text is `0` and below it is the end

Members.Name: LineOf
Members.Doc: the line an index falls on, 1-based and clamped — `index` is the number a **search** gave, so it is counted in UTF-16 units

Members.Name: Lines
Members.Doc: the lines it breaks into, as an array — for a caller that will draw them one by one. **Refused with `Markup`** — see below

Members.Name: OffsetAt
Members.Doc: the **character** offset of that line and column, clamped the way an editor's `Select` clamps

Members.Name: Size
Members.Doc: `{ Width, Height, Lines }` in **one** measurement, which is one layout instead of three

Members.Name: Width
Members.Doc: how wide it lays out, in pixels

Members.Name: Add
Members.Doc: `minutes` may be negative, and it **wraps at midnight**, because a time of day has no day to fall off

Members.Name: Between
Members.Doc: whole minutes from one to the other, signed

Members.Name: Now
Members.Doc: the time of day now, with seconds (`"21:03:58"`)

Members.Name: Seconds
Members.Doc: seconds since midnight — the exact number, for anything finer than a minute

Members.Name: After
Members.Doc: runs `tick` once after `delay` milliseconds, and answers the `Timer`, so what was started can be stopped. `Timer.After(0, fn)` is how GTK is given a frame

Members.Name: Enabled
Members.Doc: whether it is running; assigning starts or stops it

Members.Name: Every
Members.Doc: runs `tick` every `delay` milliseconds until it is stopped, and answers the `Timer`

Members.Name: Once
Members.Doc: fire one more time and stop

Members.Name: Start
Members.Doc: starts it, after `delay` when one is given, else after its own `Delay`; answers the timer

Members.Name: Stop
Members.Doc: stops it; answers the timer

Members.Name: Available
Members.Doc: whether this build has libxml2; the verbs refuse with a sentence when it does not

Members.Name: Element
Members.Doc: a detached element; its own tree, not in any document

Members.Name: Parse
Members.Doc: the document, or a `SyntaxError` naming línea and columna

Members.Name: ParseBytes
Members.Doc: the same, and the declaration's encoding is honoured — what `File.LoadXml` uses

Members.Name: Schema
Members.Doc: compiles an XSD **once** -- from its text, a document or an element in one -- so a file can be checked as often as it arrives. A schema that includes or imports another document is refused, because compiling it would fetch a file or an URL from inside what is meant to be a check; `Validate` is the question and it never writes to the document

Members.Name: Stringify
Members.Doc: the canonical text: declaration, indented by two, one trailing newline. A detached element is written with a document of its own

Members.Name: Create
Members.Doc: starts an archive that will be at `path` **when `Finish()` says so** and not before: it is written to a temporary beside it, so a failure, an abort or a dropped writer leaves nothing and an existing file untouched. Throws, naming the folder, when it cannot write there

Members.Name: Open
Members.Doc: reads the archive's directory and answers a handle on it. Throws, naming the file and the reason, for anything that is not a zip, is cut short, is zip64 or split over disks, or lists one name twice. An archive up to 32 MiB is held in memory; a bigger one is mapped, so do not open one that is still being written

Members.Name: Enabled
Members.Doc: the whole reason this exists: one assignment, and every button, menu item and accelerator naming the command follows

Members.Name: EventNames
Members.Doc: the events it raises, `Execute`

Members.Name: Execute
Members.Doc: runs the command from code, as a button or an accelerator would -- raising `Execute`. **Throws while it is disabled**

Members.Name: Icon
Members.Doc: the icon the `.form` declared, lent to a control that names none

Members.Name: Name
Members.Doc: what the `.form` called the command: `this.<Name>`, `<Name>_Execute`, and what a control's `Action` names

Members.Name: PropertyNames
Members.Doc: what this class has, asked of it the way a control is asked. A command is not a widget, so nothing else can make one to ask

Members.Name: Text
Members.Doc: the label the `.form` declared. It goes through the catalogue **once**, however many places show it

Events.Name: Execute
Events.Doc: the command ran: from a control or a menu item that points at it, its accelerator, or `Execute()`. **Not raised while it is disabled**

Members.Name: Buffering
Members.Doc: how full the buffer is, `0`…`100`. `100` is nothing to wait for — a local file never says otherwise — and less is a stream refilling, which **holds the sound while `Playing` stays true**. It is [`ProgressBar.Value`](docs/reference/widgets/ProgressBar.md)'s range, since that is where a form puts it

Members.Name: Duration
Members.Doc: seconds long, `-1` while unknown — which is always, on a live stream

Members.Name: Latency
Members.Doc: ms the RTSP jitterbuffer may hold. Default `2000`, the source's own. Read when the source is built, so a change lands on the next `Play` from a stopped player

Members.Name: Loop
Members.Doc: reseek instead of ending. A live stream cannot seek, so it ends anyway

Members.Name: Muted
Members.Doc: silence without touching `Volume`, so unmuting comes back to where it was

Members.Name: OnEnded
Members.Doc: assign `() => …`, called when it plays to the end; `null` takes it off. **Anything else is refused where it is assigned**, rather than silently never called

Members.Name: OnError
Members.Doc: assign `(message, kind) => …`; the same rule. `kind` is `NotFound`, `NotAuthorized`, `Unreachable`, `Decode` or `Error`, as a `Video`'s is

Members.Name: Password
Members.Doc: the secret beside it. **Write-only**: it reads back `""` and is never serialised, so no `.form` carries it in clear text

Members.Name: Pause
Members.Doc: holds the position

Members.Name: Play
Members.Doc: plays, and replays from the top after it ended. **Refused with no `Uri`**

Members.Name: Playing
Members.Doc: whether it is going — what `Play` asked for, until `Pause`, `Stop`, the end or an error. **Not a sample of the pipeline**, which reads as stopped mid-loop and mid-rebuffer

Members.Name: Position
Members.Doc: seconds in, `0` when unknown — which includes playing live

Members.Name: Seek
Members.Doc: jumps there. **Refused on a stream that cannot seek**, naming it

Members.Name: Seekable
Members.Doc: whether `Seek` has anything to work on. Answered once the stream is known, not when playing starts

Members.Name: Stop
Members.Doc: parks it: back to no state, the position forgotten

Members.Name: Uri
Members.Doc: what to play: a URI (`file://`, `http(s)://`, `rtsp://`) **or a plain local path**, which is turned into one. One property for both, so there is nothing to disagree. Setting it stops whatever was playing

Members.Name: User
Members.Doc: RTSP digest identity, applied to the source the playbin builds. `""` for none

Members.Name: Close
Members.Doc: let it go

Members.Name: Columns
Members.Doc: `[{ Name, Type, Required, Key }]` — what is really in the table, which is how a program checks that a record's shape still fits

Members.Name: Dialect
Members.Doc: `{ Placeholder, Quote, NewKey }` — **what differs per engine**, so the portable half above can build SQL without knowing which engine it is talking to

Members.Name: Execute
Members.Doc: **one** statement, answering `{ Changes, LastId }`

Members.Name: Open
Members.Doc: whether it still is

Members.Name: Path
Members.Doc: the file this connection is

Members.Name: Query
Members.Doc: the rows a statement answers, as **plain objects** — for the report, the `GROUP BY`, the join that is not one shape

Members.Name: Script
Members.Doc: several statements and **no parameters**: a schema, a migration

Members.Name: Table
Members.Doc: a [`Table`](docs/reference/globals/Database.md): the rows of `name` as records of `Shape`

Members.Name: Tables
Members.Doc: the tables and views, ordered

Members.Name: Transaction
Members.Doc: everything in `fn` or nothing. **Nests**, through savepoints, so a function that wraps its own work in one is safe to call from inside another

Members.Name: Auth
Members.Doc: `{ User, Password }`, Basic and preemptive; reads back `null` when none is set. An explicit `Authorization` header wins over it, and an explicit `Content-Type` header wins over the one the body's shape implies

Members.Name: BaseUrl
Members.Doc: what a relative path in a call is relative to, so the program's requests are one-liners

Members.Name: Cookies
Members.Doc: `false` unless told: `true` keeps a jar of the session's own, so a login answers the next request

Members.Name: Delete
Members.Doc: no body, like `Get`

Members.Name: DeleteWait
Members.Doc: the blocking `Delete`

Members.Name: FollowRedirects
Members.Doc: follow a `3xx`. Default `true`

Members.Name: Get
Members.Doc: the ordinary read

Members.Name: GetWait
Members.Doc: the blocking `Get`

Members.Name: Head
Members.Doc: the headers and no body, for *is it there* and *has it changed*

Members.Name: HeadWait
Members.Doc: the blocking `Head`

Members.Name: Headers
Members.Doc: sent with every request this client makes — an API key, an `Accept`

Members.Name: IdleTimeout
Members.Doc: ms a pooled connection idles before soup closes it (`0` is soup's own 60 s); soup counts seconds, so anything under one becomes one

Members.Name: Language
Members.Doc: the `Accept-Language` it asks with

Members.Name: Log
Members.Doc: `"none"` unless told: `"minimal"`, `"headers"` or `"body"` sends the traffic through `Logger` at `Debug` — so `Logger.Level = "Debug"` shows it and a `Handler` takes it; a `Wait`'s never reaches a `Handler`, since its context is private and its caller is blocked

Members.Name: MaxConns
Members.Doc: how many connections at once, `10` unless told. **Constructor-only**: soup takes it once, so assigning later throws

Members.Name: MaxPerHost
Members.Doc: how many of those to one host, `2` unless told. Likewise

Members.Name: Patch
Members.Doc: the same, for part of one

Members.Name: PatchWait
Members.Doc: the blocking `Patch`

Members.Name: Post
Members.Doc: `body` is text, [`Bytes`](docs/reference/globals/Bytes.md), an object (canonical JSON, `application/json`) or a [`Multipart`](docs/reference/globals/Http.md#uploads)

Members.Name: PostWait
Members.Doc: the blocking `Post`

Members.Name: Proxy
Members.Doc: what to go through

Members.Name: Put
Members.Doc: the same, for a replacement

Members.Name: PutWait
Members.Doc: the blocking `Put`

Members.Name: Request
Members.Doc: any verb: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`; anything else is refused, in the blocking spelling too

Members.Name: RequestWait
Members.Doc: the blocking spelling: answers with the record, **throws** on transport failure — and what it throws carries the same `Kind` and `Status` the callback would have been handed

Members.Name: Stream
Members.Doc: the answer **as it arrives**: `onLine(line, handle)` once per text line, the newline stripped, blank lines included. Method-first like `Request`, so a `POST` whose answer comes in pieces needs no second name

Members.Name: Timeout
Members.Doc: ms before a request is given up on; `0` waits forever

Members.Name: Tls
Members.Doc: `{ Ca, Cert }`, or nothing. `Ca` is a **certificate to verify the server's against** — the company's own CA on an internal network, or the server's own file when it is self-signed, which is exactly the case the system store cannot reach and a per-program file can. `Cert` is **the server's certificate, pinned**: it must be byte for byte that one. Either accepts; `null` when none is set.
